assertions.title: Information architecture doc — primary flow, keybinding table

steps.expected: File exists with all sections (a) through (h)
steps.observed: File exists at docs/plans/tui-redesign/information-architecture.md. All 8 sections found: (a) Three-Lane Layout Responsibilities, (b) Agent Inventory → Detail → Ask/Chat Primary Flow, (c) Rooms Secondary Flow Outline, (d) Navigation Model, (e) Focus Model, (f) Keybinding Table, (g) Screen Inventory, (h) Error / Loading / Empty State Mapping Per Screen.

steps.expected: Section specifies Main Lane, Detail Lane, and Evidence Lane with canonical responsibilities and approximate widths
steps.observed: Section (a) present with Main Lane (~40% width, agent inventory), Detail Lane (~35% width, entity details/composer), Evidence Lane (~25% width collapsible, raw payloads/events). Each lane has defined contents, empty/loading/error states, and a reconciliation table mapping prior four-region shell to three-lane model.

steps.action: Verify (b) agent inventory → detail → ask/chat primary flow
steps.expected: Screen-by-screen primary flow documented
steps.observed: Four screens documented: Screen 1 (Loading → Agent Inventory), Screen 2 (Selecting an Agent), Screen 3 (Ask/Chat with streaming), Screen 4 (Evidence Inspection). Each screen specifies triggers, behaviors, and available keyboard actions.

steps.expected: Rooms flow documented as secondary, not primary
steps.observed: Section (c) covers Rooms List (navigation via '2' key, room directory in Main lane) and Room Detail (membership, purpose, read-only in M3). Explicitly notes rooms are secondary per DESIGN.md 'Runtime First' principle.

steps.expected: Lane-based, entity-first navigation documented with global and in-lane keys
steps.observed: Section (d) defines global navigation keys (1/2/Tab/Shift+Tab/ESC/q/Ctrl+C), in-lane navigation keys (↓/j, ↑/k, Home/g, End/G, PageDown/Ctrl+D, PageUp/Ctrl+U, Enter, e), and ESC back-navigation hierarchy (drawer → composer blur → secondary screen → quit).

steps.expected: Focus indicators, cycling, and preservation documented
steps.observed: Section (e) specifies focus indicators (highlighted border, distinct background, visible cursor), focus cycling (Main → Detail → Evidence → Main), focus within lanes, and focus preservation across Tab, screen switches, and terminal resizes.

steps.action: Verify (f) keybinding table format and cross-reference
steps.expected: Table with columns: New Binding | Purpose | Conflicts with existing binding in keys.go or 'none'. All conflicts acknowledged.
steps.observed: Keybinding table has 19 rows with columns matching required format. 8 bindings marked as conflicts, all with explicit conflict source (keys.go line numbers or shell.gsx line references) and resolution/acknowledgement. 11 bindings marked 'No conflict.' Conflict Summary section explicitly lists all 8 acknowledged conflicts.

steps.action: Cross-reference keybinding table against keys.go and shell.gsx
steps.expected: No unacknowledged conflicts between IA table and actual code
steps.observed: Verified all 19 bindings against keys.go (lines 38-40: ESC→App().Stop(), q→App().Stop(), Ctrl+C→App().Stop()) and shell.gsx (lines 269-311: FocusGroup KeyMap for Tab/Shift+Tab, Ctrl+M→setRail(RailMemory), Ctrl+Y→setRail(RailContinuity), Ctrl+W→setRail(RailWorkers), Ctrl+B→setRail(RailTask), Enter→submitComposer, Ctrl+X→submitCancel). All conflicts in the IA table match actual code. Minor note: shell.gsx also binds KeyRight→cycleRail(1) and KeyLeft→cycleRail(-1) which the IA table does not mention. These rail-cycling bindings are implicitly superseded by the three-lane model (no rail tabs), so omission is defensible but not explicitly acknowledged.

steps.expected: Table listing all screens with Main/Detail/Evidence lane contents and navigation
steps.observed: 8-screen inventory table: Agent Inventory, Agent Detail, Ask/Chat, Rooms Directory, Loading, Connection Error, Empty Daemon, Too Small. Each screen specifies Main Lane, Detail Lane, Evidence Lane contents and navigation trigger.

steps.action: Verify (h) error/loading/empty state mapping per screen
steps.expected: Table mapping each screen's loading, empty, and error states
steps.observed: 7-row state mapping table covering Agent Inventory, Agent Detail, Ask/Chat, Rooms Directory, Evidence Drawer, Status Footer, and Too Small Guard. Each row specifies Loading State, Empty State, and Error State with descriptive text. State Design Rules section adds 4 constraints per DESIGN.md accessibility requirements.

sections_found.(a): Three-Lane Layout Responsibilities — present with lane definitions, widths, contents, states, and reconciliation table
sections_found.(b): Agent Inventory → Detail → Ask/Chat Primary Flow — 4 screens with triggers, behaviors, keyboard actions
sections_found.(c): Rooms Secondary Flow Outline — rooms list and room detail as secondary screens
sections_found.(d): Navigation Model — global keys, in-lane keys, back navigation hierarchy
sections_found.(e): Focus Model — indicators, cycling, within-lane, preservation rules
sections_found.(f): Keybinding Table — 19 rows, 8 conflicts acknowledged, Conflict Summary section
sections_found.(g): Screen Inventory — 8-screen table with lane contents and navigation
sections_found.(h): Error/Loading/Empty State Mapping — 7-row table + State Design Rules

keybinding_cross_reference.note: shell.gsx KeyRight (cycleRail) and KeyLeft (cycleRail) bindings not in IA table; implicitly superseded by lane model but not explicitly acknowledged

assertions.title: IA specifies progressive reveal for summary-first / raw-second

steps.expected: Section exists with a 4-row mapping covering transcript rows, tool activity, events, and errors
steps.observed: 'Progressive Reveal' section found (after section (h)). Contains a 4-column table (Category, Summary Default, User Action to Expose Raw, Raw View) with exactly 4 rows covering all required categories.

steps.expected: Summary default and user action specified for transcript rows
steps.observed: Summary Default: 'Single-line summary: speaker label, entry kind badge (ask/reply/tool/error/status), truncated text to fit width. Tool calls show tool name + "…" only. Errors show "⚠ <message>" truncated.' User Action: 'Press e on the selected row to open the Evidence drawer.' Raw View: 'Full text content for replies; full JSON args + result for tool calls; full error code + message + stack trace for errors; complete metadata (correlation ID, timestamps).'

steps.expected: Summary default and user action specified for tool activity
steps.observed: Summary Default: 'Inline collapsed row in transcript: tool name + status badge (running ✓/✗/⏳) + one-line result summary. Arguments hidden.' User Action: 'Press e on the tool row, or press → to expand inline.' Raw View: 'Full argument JSON (syntax-highlighted key/value pairs), full result JSON, duration, exit code. Scrollable within the drawer.'

steps.expected: Summary default and user action specified for events
steps.observed: Summary Default: 'Curated event list filtered to errors and notable signals (agent spawned, agent killed, connection state change). Each event is one line with timestamp + type + summary.' User Action: 'Press e on an event row, or navigate to Events in the Evidence drawer.' Raw View: 'Full event JSON payload, including all metadata fields. Filterable by topic within the drawer.'

steps.expected: Summary default and user action specified for errors
steps.observed: Summary Default: 'Error badge in transcript rows and status footer: "⚠ <short message>". Error count shown in footer.' User Action: 'Press e on the error row, or open the Evidence drawer filtered to errors.' Raw View: 'Full error: code, message, stack trace, HTTP status if applicable, request URL, correlation ID, suggested fix from data.hint.'

steps.action: Verify Progressive Reveal Design Rules section
steps.expected: Additional rules supporting the progressive reveal model
steps.observed: 4 rules present: (1) Never require raw payload reading to understand basic state. (2) One-key access via 'e'. (3) Drawer preserves context. (4) No raw JSON as primary UI per DESIGN.md.

evidence.section_found: Progressive Reveal section with 4-row × 4-column table covering all categories (transcript rows, tool activity, events, errors) plus 4 Progressive Reveal Design Rules

assertions.title: IA preserves three-plane memory model from canonical plan

steps.action: Find 'Three-Plane Memory Model' section in information-architecture.md
steps.expected: Section exists naming Companion Memory, Named Durable Memory, and ACA/Continuity as three distinct surfaces
steps.observed: 'Three-Plane Memory Model' section found (after Progressive Reveal). Contains three named subsections: 'Companion Memory', 'Named Durable Memory', and 'ACA / Continuity'. Introductory text states: 'the shell must preserve separation between three memory planes. These planes are not merged into one generic "memory" list.'

steps.action: Verify Companion Memory subsection specifies cockpit surface and projection/heuristic labeling
steps.expected: Specifies which cockpit surface exposes this plane and includes projection/heuristic labeling per DESIGN.md Honest Surfaces
steps.observed: Cockpit surface: 'Evidence drawer under the "Memory" sub-tab (accessible via Ctrl+M).' Shows Injected Now, Search, Stats. Projection/heuristic labeling: 'The "Injected Now" view is a **projection** — it represents the companion service's assembled context at a point in time, not a canonical record. Per DESIGN.md "Honest Surfaces" principle, the UI labels this as "Assembled context — what the model will remember if you send a prompt right now."' Heuristic ranking labeled 'Relevance score (heuristic)' rather than ground truth.

steps.action: Verify Named Durable Memory subsection specifies cockpit surface and projection/heuristic labeling
steps.expected: Specifies which cockpit surface exposes this plane and includes projection/heuristic labeling
steps.observed: Cockpit surface: 'Evidence drawer under a "Durable Memory" sub-section within the Memory tab.' Shows search, list by type, stats. Projection/heuristic labeling: 'Search results are ranked by semantic similarity, which is a **heuristic**. Per DESIGN.md "Honest Surfaces," the UI labels search results with "Similarity: <score>" and shows the match type (semantic, exact, tag) explicitly. The UI does not present ranked results as if they are an authoritative or canonical ordering.'

steps.action: Verify ACA / Continuity subsection specifies cockpit surface and projection/heuristic labeling
steps.expected: Specifies which cockpit surface exposes this plane and includes projection/heuristic labeling
steps.observed: Cockpit surface: 'Evidence drawer under the "Continuity" sub-tab (accessible via Ctrl+Y).' Shows top-of-mind summary, task-history summary, latest handoff, open tensions/observations, family-history summary. Projection/heuristic labeling: ACA summaries labeled 'ACA summary — synthesized from session timeline and memory artifacts' (projected, not canonical). Handoff records labeled 'Stored handoff' (canonical). Tensions labeled 'From ACA observations' (machine-extracted) vs 'Operator-logged' (manual) to show provenance.

subsections_found.Companion Memory: Present. Cockpit surface: Evidence drawer Memory sub-tab. Projection labeling: 'Assembled context — what the model will remember if you send a prompt right now'. Heuristic labeling: 'Relevance score (heuristic)'.
subsections_found.Named Durable Memory: Present. Cockpit surface: Evidence drawer Durable Memory sub-section. Heuristic labeling: 'Similarity: <score>' with match type shown.
subsections_found.ACA / Continuity: Present. Cockpit surface: Evidence drawer Continuity sub-tab. Projection labeling: 'ACA summary — synthesized from session timeline and memory artifacts'. Provenance labeling: 'From ACA observations' vs 'Operator-logged'.

evidence.projection_heuristic_labeling: All three planes include at least one sentence covering projection/heuristic labeling per DESIGN.md 'Honest Surfaces' principle.

summary: Tested 3 assertions: all 3 passed. VAL-DOCS-004: All 8 sections (a)-(h) present with required content. Keybinding table has 19 rows with proper format; all 8 conflicts cross-referenced against keys.go and shell.gsx are acknowledged. Minor note: KeyRight/KeyLeft rail-cycling bindings in shell.gsx are not explicitly acknowledged as being superseded. VAL-DOCS-011: Progressive Reveal section contains complete 4-row mapping for transcript rows, tool activity, events, and errors with Summary Default, User Action, and Raw View columns. VAL-DOCS-013: Three-Plane Memory Model section has all three named subsections (Companion Memory, Named Durable Memory, ACA/Continuity), each specifying cockpit surface and projection/heuristic labeling per DESIGN.md Honest Surfaces.
